unit: Geometry · Chapter II. Perpendicularity, distances and angles

stages.headline: If a line in the plane is perpendicular to the projection of an oblique, it is perpendicular to the oblique; the converse also holds.
stages.headlineEnglish: If a line in the plane is perpendicular to the projection of an oblique, it is perpendicular to the oblique; the converse also holds.

stages.headline: Application: SA ⊥ (ABC) at vertex A of square ABCD. Since AB ⊥ BC, the theorem gives SB ⊥ BC, so the distance from S to BC is SB.
stages.headlineEnglish: Application: SA ⊥ (ABC) at vertex A of square ABCD. Since AB ⊥ BC, the theorem gives SB ⊥ BC, so the distance from S to BC is SB.

stages.headline: Example: side 4 and SA = 3 give the distance from S to BC: SB = √(9 + 16) = 5.
stages.headlineEnglish: Example: side 4 and SA = 3 give the distance from S to BC: SB = √(9 + 16) = 5.
